title: The year the Sun turned blood red over Europe 🌋
subject: volcano
description:
Could a volcano do this again today? 👇

In 1783, Iceland's Laki fissure erupted for about 8 months. Its sulfur haze spread over most of Europe and as far as Syria, the Sun looked blood red at sunrise and sunset, and the Haze Famine that followed killed about one-fifth of Iceland's people.

Sources: Encyclopaedia Britannica ("Laki"), Encyclopédie de l'environnement ("The Laki Fissure eruption, 1783-1784"), Scientific American ("How the Laki eruptions changed history")

scenes.text: The Sun turned blood red over Europe.
A strange dry fog had spread across the continent, reaching as far as Syria.
It came from Iceland, where a volcanic fissure called Laki tore open on June 8, 1783.
But here's the strange part. It wasn't one big blast. For 8 months, it kept pouring out lava and poisonous gas.
The gas killed half of Iceland's cattle and most of its sheep and horses.
In the famine that followed, about 1 in 5 Icelanders died.
